The commands `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will only download and extract the source using the provided URL and checksum, without executing any build or prepare steps. No malicious or suspicious operations occur during sourcing of the PKGBUILD. Standard AUR practices are followed.
</details>

Dependencies and provides/conflicts are appropriately declared for a 32-bit NVIDIA utility package. No network operations, file manipulations, or system modifications are performed by this file itself.

The PKGBUILD file is for a 32-bit NVIDIA driver utility package in the AUR, targeting the 580xx series. The `sha512sums` checksum ensures the integrity of the downloaded file, and the checksum value is provided inline, not marked as 'SKIP'. This indicates a trusted source verification.

The build process involves extracting the NVIDIA `.run` file and installing specific libraries into the 32-bit library directory. All installed components are standard NVIDIA GPU-related libraries (OpenGL, Vulkan, CUDA, VDPAU, etc.), consistent with the package description. The `create_links` function creates standard shared library symlinks (SONAME links), a common packaging practice to support dynamic linking.

No network operations, code downloads, or executions occur at runtime or during build beyond the initial source fetch. There are no obfuscated commands, suspicious file operations, or attempts to exfiltrate data. All operations are confined to the build directory and target package directory (`$pkgdir`). The package replaces and conflicts with related NVIDIA packages appropriately, following standard driver packaging conventions. No AUR helper scripts or post-install hooks exhibit malicious behavior.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines only static variables and function definitions at the top level. There is no `pkgver()` function—the version is set as a literal string. The `source` array fetches the NVIDIA driver `.run` file directly from the official NVIDIA download server (`https://download.nvidia.com/XFree86/Linux-x86_64/...`), which is the expected upstream. A SHA-512 checksum is provided for verification. No top-level code executes any dangerous commands, and the `prepare()`, `build()`, and `package()` functions (which contain file operations) are not invoked by `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`. Therefore, fetching the source and sourcing the PKGBUILD is safe.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>

</security_assessment>
